sources.title: SBI Holdings release identifying SBI Capital Co., Ltd. as SBIC
claims: SBI Holdings identifies its consolidated subsidiary SBI Capital Co., Ltd. as 'SBIC' in the release.
The context is an investment fund and portfolio-company share transaction.
limitations: This is a historical entity and abbreviation usage; it does not identify Tokyo SBIC East Japan.
It does not establish a current XRP, Ripple, Coinbase or Circle relationship.

sources.title: SBI Holdings forms buy-out investment alliance with Goldman Sachs
claims: SBI Holdings announced a joint venture for buy-out investment in Japanese middle-sized companies.
The release says SBI would transfer 40% of SBI Capital Co., Ltd. to a Goldman Sachs group company.
limitations: The announcement describes the 2007 ownership transaction; it does not establish the exact later transfer date or current entity status.

sources.title: SBI Capital ownership and buy-out fund activity
claims: The release describes SBI Capital as a joint venture with 60% held by SBI Holdings and 40% by a Goldman Sachs group company.
SBI Capital's purpose was investment in middle-market public and private companies and enterprise-value improvement.
limitations: The source is a historical 2007 snapshot, not a current ownership record.

sources.title: Establishment of intermediate holding companies through joint share transfer
claims: SBI Holdings announced SBI Capital Management Co., Ltd. as an intermediate holding company for asset-management subsidiaries.
The 2012-03-31 table lists SBI Capital Co., Ltd. as 100% owned by SBI Holdings and describes its business as managing buy-out and corporate-revitalization funds.
limitations: The release does not explain the exact transaction or date by which the 2007 Goldman 40% interest ceased to appear in the 2012 ownership table.
Do not infer uninterrupted ownership or the transfer date from these two snapshots.
